diffusion_derivative: N/A (multi-dimensional, m=13 non-commuting channels; scalar Milstein not applicable)
milstein_correction: N/A. Multi-dimensional Milstein requires the Levy areas (iterated integrals int int dW_i dW_j) because the diffusion generators do not commute ([M1, M2] != 0). Use Euler-Maruyama; refine dt to control the multiplicative-noise variance bias.

analytic_moments.second_moment_ode: The second-moment matrix P(t) = E[X X^T] solves dP/dt = F P + P F^T + sum_r G_r P G_r^T with P(0) = X0 X0^T = [[1,1],[1,1]]. Because M1 P M1^T = [[P22,0],[0,0]] and M2 P M2^T = [[0,0],[0,P11]], the diffusion sum reduces to diag(0.36*7*P22, 0.36*6*P11) = diag(2.52*P22, 2.16*P11). Vectorizing the symmetric entries as p = (P11, P12, P22) gives the closed linear system dp/dt = A p with A = [[-4, 6, 2.52], [-3, -4, 3], [2.16, -6, -4]], so p(t) = expm(A*t) @ (1,1,1).

implementation_notes: 2D linear Ito system driven by m=13 independent Brownian motions with multiplicative (state-dependent) noise. State layout: terminal_paths shape (num_paths, 2), column 0 = X, column 1 = Y. SCHEME: use Euler-Maruyama (vector form). Multi-dimensional Milstein is NOT available because the diffusion generators are non-commuting ([M1, M2] != 0), which would require simulating Levy areas. Assemble the noise correctly: 7 odd channels use G = 0.6*M1 = [[0, 0.6], [0, 0]] and 6 even channels use G = 0.6*M2 = [[0, 0], [0.6, 0]]. Draw 13 independent N(0,1) increments per step (or, since the 7 odd channels are identical and the 6 even channels are identical, the aggregate increment can be formed as 0.6*M1*sqrt(7)*Z_odd and 0.6*M2*sqrt(6)*Z_even with two independent standard normals Z_odd, Z_even per step per path — this is exactly equivalent in law and much cheaper). Per-path EM step: dX_drift = (F @ X)*dt; dX_noise = sum_r 0.6 * (M_r @ X) * dW_r. STIFFNESS/STEP SIZE: F has eigenvalues -2 +/- 3i (spiral decay, |lambda| ~ 3.6) and the multiplicative noise is strong, so the terminal variance is sensitive to dt. Use a small step (e.g. dt <= 0.005, refine until the variance error stabilizes); a semi-implicit treatment of the drift can help stability. EXACT MOMENTS: mean = expm(F*T) @ X0 (closed form given above); variances come from the second-moment matrix P(t) = expm(A*t) @ (1,1,1) with the 3x3 generator A above, then Var_X = P11 - mean_X^2, Var_Y = P22 - mean_Y^2. At T=1: mean_X = -0.11488, mean_Y = -0.15308 (both |mean| > 0.01 so the mean check applies), Var_X = 0.17160, Var_Y = 0.16272. Both components must pass variance and mean checks for overall PASS.
